question: In the final moment, Harry suddenly looks wide-eyed and startled after Poby finally speaks up in the quiet room. Based on the scene and their conversation, what most likely caused Harry’s surprised reaction?

options.text: Poby says his loud singing is making it hard to think.

options.label: B
options.text: Poby praises his performance and asks for an encore.

options.label: C
options.text: Poby suddenly starts singing along with the same melody.

dialog.text: La-la-laaa! What a perfect night for a song, right by your cozy bed, Poby!
dialog.speaker: Harry

dialog.text: Mm-hmm… it does sound nice, Harry. The cabin feels extra quiet outside tonight.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: And inside it’s filled with my sparkling high notes! Listen to this part—ta-da-DAAA!
dialog.speaker: Harry

dialog.text: Ah… that’s very… lively. I’ve been up all day fixing things around here, so my head’s a bit fuzzy.

dialog.text: Oh! Then I’ll give you an even grander finale to wake you up—this next verse is the loudest one!
dialog.speaker: Harry

dialog.text: Actually, Harry… it’s really late now, and my eyes won’t stay open. I’m having trouble keeping my thoughts straight with all the… high notes.

dialog.text: Wait—seriously? You mean I’ve been belting this out while you were trying to wind down?
dialog.speaker: Harry

question: Based on the audio, why do Crong and Eddy stop being upset with Pororo at the end?

options.label: A
options.text: They notice Pororo turning the situation into a joke and changing the subject away from the damaged sled.

options.label: B
options.text: They hear Pororo say the sled is still cracked and that someone else is the one who should fix it.

options.label: C
options.text: They realize Pororo made a mistake with Crong’s sled, already repaired it, and is now explaining this openly.

options.label: D
options.text: They see that Pororo still insists nothing was his fault and refuses to admit he damaged the sled.

dialog.text: Pororo, what do you mean that wasn’t my sled you took? You just said you borrowed it like it was nothing!
dialog.speaker: Crong

dialog.text: I know it sounded that way, Crong, but let me explain.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: Explain? You scratched it, left it out in the snow, and now you’re saying it’s no big deal?
dialog.speaker: Crong

dialog.text: Hold on, Pororo. Crong told me you zoomed off on his sled and crashed it. Were you just pretending it wasn’t your fault?
dialog.speaker: Eddy

dialog.text: Yeah! You were laughing when you said it, like it was some kind of joke.
dialog.speaker: Crong

dialog.text: I wasn’t joking. I borrowed a sled from the hill, remember the extra ones by the tree? I thought it was an old spare. I only found out later it was the one you had just painted, Crong.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: Wait, so you didn’t just grab Crong’s on purpose? You thought it was one of the community sleds?
dialog.speaker: Eddy

dialog.text: Exactly. When I saw the new paint, I went back, checked the marks on the bottom, and realized it was yours. That’s why I fixed the crack and wiped it down before you came back.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: You… already fixed it?
dialog.speaker: Crong

dialog.text: Yeah. I came by to tell you, but you asked me if I took it and I answered too fast. It must have sounded like I didn’t care, but I was just trying to say it was a mistake and it’s okay now.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: So that’s why there was a new brace under the sled… I thought I imagined that.
dialog.speaker: Eddy

dialog.text: I should’ve explained from the start instead of sounding casual. If you still want, we can test it together down the hill and see if it rides even smoother now.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: …Down the hill together, huh?
dialog.speaker: Crong

question: Why does Pororo urgently tell Harry, "Don’t come up here, just stay at your house where it’s safe"?

dialog.speaker: Crong

dialog.speaker: Crong

dialog.text: Yeah… we can’t jump, and turning around on this narrow ledge is really risky.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: Hey, you two! Are you still climbing? The view looks great from here!
dialog.speaker: Harry

dialog.text: Is that Harry? He’s down by his house, crong!

dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: Do you want me to come up and help you?

question: In the last scene, Poby is no longer round and is floating more like his usual self instead of a giant balloon. What most likely caused him to return to his normal size?

options.label: A
options.text: Gas slowly leaking out as he moves in the air

options.label: B
options.text: A sudden magic spell returning him to normal

options.label: C
options.text: Someone popping him at once with a sharp object

options.label: D
options.text: Getting slimmer from exercise and healthy habits

dialog.text: Ah-choo… ah… ah… nope. Ugh, it still won’t come out. I feel like a giant balloon!
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: You really do look like one. Are you still packed full of gas?
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: Yeah. I thought a big sneeze would blast it all out, but I can’t sneeze on purpose.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: Okay, forget the sneeze. What if we let it out slowly instead of all at once?
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: Slowly? How do I do that when I’m already stuck like this?
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: You’re so light from the gas that you’re floating anyway. Try moving around up there—stretch, twist, spin a bit. Maybe the gas will find tiny ways to escape while you float.

dialog.text: So… just keep drifting and wiggling in the air, and let it leak bit by bit?
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: Exactly! Don’t force it, just stay in motion. I’ll watch from down here to make sure you’re okay.
dialog.speaker: Pororo

dialog.text: All right, here goes. I’m turning… and stretching… whoa, I feel kind of different already.

dialog.text: I’m not sure… my fur isn’t as tight, and the wind feels stronger under me. Something’s definitely changing!
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: High above the ground, Poby drifts across the sky, his round body no longer quite as huge, as he slowly moves through the clouds.

dialog.text: Eddy… we’re trapped on this sagging part of the bridge!

dialog.text: Hi, Petty! The snow is really piling up today.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: Hey, Poby! It looks beautiful out here. Have you been outside long?
dialog.speaker: Petty

dialog.text: Just came out to stretch a bit. I didn’t want to miss saying hello when I saw you at the door.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: That’s sweet of you. Don’t stay in the cold too long, though. You’ll freeze out here!
dialog.speaker: Petty

dialog.text: You’re right, it’s getting chilly. I’ll head inside for a bit and warm up.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: Ah, much better… Oh, Harry, you’re by the window again.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: I like watching the snow fall from here. It’s so calm.
dialog.speaker: Harry

dialog.text: It does look peaceful from inside. You’ve got the best spot in the house.
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: And you look a lot warmer now too.
dialog.speaker: Harry

dialog.text: I do. Mind if I stay here and chat with you for a while, Harry?
dialog.speaker: Poby

dialog.text: Not at all. Tell me what’s on your mind, Poby.

dialog.text: Sure… let’s just sit here and talk while the snow keeps falling.

dialog.text: Maybe I should come closer and look.

dialog.text: Okay, I’m coming over. Don’t move it yet!
dialog.speaker: Crong
